subject: Weekly runway: assign GPU bandwidth per-account (Q4 tranche)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly runway: assign GPU bandwidth per-account (Q4 tranche)

Team —

Putting a short ask in advance of today's capacity sync. Goal: lock GPU slot assignments for the next 60 days so Sales/Finance/Infra can book or repurpose capacity before the end-of-quarter closes. I attached a simple spreadsheet (Q4_account_slots.xlsx) with the accounts I think need dedicated slots. Quick summary below (top-of-sheet):

- Acme AI — est 20 dedicated slot-hours/day; target close 2025-09-25; priority: 1; region: us-west
- Globex — est 8 slots/day; target close 2025-10-10; priority: 2; region: us-east (preference for reserved burst)
- Novus Labs — pilot 4 slots/day (30d pilot); target close 2025-10-02; priority: 3; region: eu-central

Asks:
1) Finance: confirm whether we have headroom for the Acme commit if it converts in early October (I put a placeholder $/slot in the sheet).
2) Infra: confirm whether those slot sizes map to our Dedicated pool A/B/C or whether we should recommend a quantified-burst (smaller footprint + burst credits).
3) Sales: if there are any close risks or scope changes, flag them here so we don't over-provision.

Can you all review and drop comments in the sheet by EOD? If anything needs an immediate call, say so and I'll pull the thread into a 20-min bridge.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly runway: assign GPU bandwidth per-account (Q4 tranche)

Ben — thanks for pulling this together. I skimmed the spreadsheet and attached a two-slide heatmap that maps the current committed budget vs. requested (deal_heatmap.pdf). A few finance notes:

- We have ~12% flexible capacity in the monthly reserved budget for September; that could cover a small Acme ramp, but anything >15% over baseline will require reallocation or an increase to the reserved spend.
- Recommended holdback: keep 10% of pool capacity unallocated for churn/benchmark tests.
- For Globex: if procurement requires a multi-month commit, we should push for a start date aligned to their PO (to reduce interim churn).

Questions:
- Is Acme expecting a multi-quarter commit or a pilot-to-commit (i.e., 30d pilot then conversion)? The commercial structure drives how Finance prefers we tier slots.

If useful, I can be on the bridge at 11:30 to run through the budget scenarios.

—Laura
Director, Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly runway: assign GPU bandwidth per-account (Q4 tranche)

Thanks — I reviewed the sheet and added inline notes in the Drive doc (link below). Operational constraints / recommendations:

- Lead time: provisioning new Dedicated pools (adding a fresh node group) is ~7 business days if we use existing spot-eligible inventory; full reserved capacity ordering + onboarding is ~4–6 weeks.
- GPU type mapping: Acme's latency needs suggest p4d or equivalent — recommend pool A (low-latency, high-memory). Globex can live on p4d-lite (pool B) with burst credits for spikes. Novus pilot: small gpus (q4) in pool C is fine.
- Suggested immediate moves: carve 12 slot-hours/day from pool A for Acme as a soft hold (no billing change yet) and set an auto-eviction if actual consumption <40% for two consecutive weeks. That gives Sales runway without over-committing.

I added a short runbook (provisioning_playbook.md) in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1GxQ_account_slotting_doc

If Finance confirms headroom, Infra can spin up the soft hold today. Otherwise we can schedule the hard provisioning after PO approval.

-Kim
Principal Infra PM, Serving Platform | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, sarah.jenkins@acme.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly runway: assign GPU bandwidth per-account (Q4 tranche)

Thanks everyone — useful callouts. Quick consolidation and next steps: 

- Finance: Laura to confirm whether we can use the ~12% flexible pool for an Acme soft hold; if yes, Kim will create the soft hold by EOD and tag it DEAL-1935.
- Infra: Kim to set auto-eviction rule (40% consumption threshold) for the soft hold and document the telemetry hooks in the runbook.
- Sales (me): I'll update the deck and confirm Acme's expected conversion model today (pilot -> commit vs. immediate commit) and loop Procurement if we need PO timing.

Sarah (Acme) — looping you in so your team sees the proposed soft hold. Can you confirm whether Acme expects a 30d pilot or a 3-month initial commitment? A short reply with "pilot" or "3-month" is fine.

Attachments: Q4_account_slots.xlsx (internal), deal_heatmap.pdf (internal)

If there are no objections, we'll treat this as the runway plan and start the soft hold today pending Finance OK.

Ben
Senior Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
